title: CRLR/260/2019 of NEMPAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 260 of 2019
Nempal
 ...Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Another
...Respondents
Mr. Bilal Ahmed, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent no. 1.
Mr. Aakib Ahmed, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the
respondent no. 2.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
A very peculiar situation has arisen in the present
criminal revision to be considered by this Court. Though the actual
controversy involved in the matter happens to be centering around a
very narrow compass, but the controversy, which as of now has
actually germinated and which requires a judicial consideration is
pertaining to the compliance to the order dated 01.07.2019, whereby,
this Court had directed the parties to the criminal revision to put in
appearance before the Lok Adalat, which was scheduled to be held on
13.07.2019 for making an effort of an amicable settlement, by way of
mediation.
2. The revisionist contends that on the scheduled date, i.e.
13.07.2019, he was in fact present before the Lok Adalat and an
endorsement to the said effect has been made by him in the order
sheet to fortify his presence. On the contrary, there is an affidavit filed
by the respondent-wife to the effect that on the scheduled date for
conducting the Lok Adalat, i.e. 13.07.2019 she has rather put in
appearance and the revisionist in fact was not present and thus she
tried to refute the contention of amicable settlement, which has been
expressed on 19.06.2018 in C482 Application No. 991 of 2018. What
she wants to contend, that the expression given by the revisionist with
regards to the possibility of an amicable settlement in C482
application is absolutely a false and farce statement for the reason,
that had there been any sanctity with regards to the intention of the

2
revisionist to enter into a settlement, he should have participated in the
Lok Adalat proceedings.
3. On this contradictory stand taken by the parties
pertaining to as to who has actually appeared before the Lok Adalat
proceedings, there are contradictory stands taken from the view point
that the revisionist contends that in the order sheet he has made an
endorsement, which was to fortify that he has actually appeared
before the Lok Adalat on 13.07.2019 and participated in the
proceeding before it, whereas, if on a simplicitor comparison of the
signature of the revisionist appearing in the order sheet and that in the
affidavit filed in support of the revision, this Court is prima-facie of
the view that the signatures do not tally with one another and there is
vast difference in the endorsements made by him at the two places.
4. Even on this aspect pertaining to as to whether the parties
have actually appeared before the Lok Adalat or not on the said date,
the Registrar (Judicial) was called upon by this Court, and he has
placed before the Court the report of the Registrar, who was
conducting the Lok Adalat on the said date. The Registrar, who was
conducting the Lok Adalat use to make an endorsement in the cause
list of the said date with regards to fortifying as to which of the parties
have put in appearance for participation of the Lok Adalat
proceedings.
5. After having gone through the said list as supplied and
produced by the Registrar before this Court, on its perusal, it does not
support the endorsement made in the order sheet about the presence of
the revisionist and further more, the said list also does not support the
contents of the affidavit as well, as filed by the respondent to show
that rather she was present on the said date and the revisionist was not
present. In such a circumstances of contradictory version coming
forward with regards to the actual participation of the parties in the
proceedings before the Lok Adalat, this Court at present is not

3
venturing into the propriety or the diligence of participation on
13.07.2019.
6. In such an eventuality, since this revision itself is arising
out of an order, which has been passed by the Family Court, Roorkee,
District Haridwar, in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No. 132 of 2018
'Pooja vs. Nempal', which was being initiated by respondent no. 2 by
invoking the provisions contained under Section 125, the learned
Family Court while considering the application for grant of interim
maintenance under sub-section (2) of Section 125 of Cr.P.C., which
was registered as paper no. 7B. It is a settled preposition that when the
parties agreed to the fact that their marriage did stood solemnized
amongst them on 15.04.2012, as per the Hindu rights and rituals and
when it is contended by the respondent no. 2 that she was virtually
thrown out of the matrimonial home after being accused and
physically assaulted on 23.02.2017 even so much so she has also
contended to the extent that the said act of forceful throwing her out
from matrimonial home, which was followed by detaining of the child
with the revisionist and the child still continues to be there with the
revisionist in his custody.
6. In order to substantiate, with regards to the determination
of the amount of maintenance, she has contended that the
respondent/husband at present is working as a doctor and has got a
sufficient income to maintain, respondent no. 2 in accordance with the
demand which she has raised in the application under Section 125(2).
All these vitalities relating thereto about the gravity of the claim,
gravity oft the income accruing to the revisionist, the entitlement of
the maintenance to the revisionist are the questions, which entails an
appreciation of evidence and its rightful appreciation by the Court, but
since under the given set of circumstances, where the court has held
that since as of now there admittedly exists a marriage dated
15.04.2012, which has not yet been dissolved, and since the court
below has only fixed an interim maintenance to be payable by the
revisionist at the rate of Rs. 4,000/- per month, this Court is of the
view that since it is only an interim arrangement made to meet a

4
particular contingency during the pendency of case so as to tied away
the financial crises of respondent no. 2, it would be in the interest of
justice that the revision itself should be dismissed, with the request to
the Family Court, Haridwar, to decide the main application under
Section 125 itself on its own merits, within a period of three months
from the date of production of certified copy of this order and for the
period of three months the revisionist will continue to remit a sum of
Rs. 4,000/- to respondent no. 2 as directed by the court below.
7. In view of the peculiar circumstances, which has
emerged in this case to determine as to which party to the proceedings
before the Lok Adalat has put in appearance or not there hade been a
contradictory records, which has been placed before this Court.
Hence, it becomes necessary for this to lay down certain wider
guidelines for the Registrar, for being followed at the time when the
proceedings before the Lok Adlat is being conducted by the Registrar.
Thus, the Registrar is hereby directed to:
(i) To notify the dates to the parties to the
proceedings, which are placed before the Lok
Adalat much prior in time giving them an
information about the date of their appearance.
(ii) On appearance to the parties to the proceedings
before Lok Adalat their presence would be
recorded by an officer to be nominated by the head
of the Lok Adalat in order to fortify as to which
party has put in appearance and in which case the
presence to be also certified by the counsel, if he is
appearing on the date.
(iii) The presence of the parties has to be recorded in
the proceedings of the order sheet of each case in
which they have been called upon in the Lok
Adalat.
(iv) The parties appearing in the proceedings will be
called upon to duly endorse their presence in the
presence of the officer conducting Lok Adalat and

5
their presence would also be certified by the
officer, who is recording their presence.
8. Let the copy of this order be sent to the Registrar
General, for necessary compliance in the forthcoming Lok Adalats so
that this controversy pertaining to as to which of the parties has
actually participated in the proceedings of the Lok Adalat on the
scheduled date or not, it may be easily determined on the perusal of
the record of the case when on a failure of the proceedings of the Lok
Adalat, it is placed before the court for its further determination.
9. Subject to the above observation, the present criminal
revision lacks merit and the same stands dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 18.09.2019
Pooja
